memory_update.text: PLPC should be carried forward as the primary underfollowed candidate for the transmission-line hardware node because its product catalog and external research directly match clamps, dead-ends, OPGW hardware, anchoring/control hardware, and utility-qualified line components.

HUBB should be retained as a reference benchmark, not the main underfollowed lane, because Hubbell Power Systems has direct transmission connector and fitting overlap but the company is much larger and broader.
AZZ is a second-order underfollowed candidate for coatings/galvanizing of T&D structures and components; survival in later layers depends on quantifying utility/T&D revenue exposure.
VMI is an adjacent transmission-structures reference name rather than a direct fittings/clamps candidate; use it to benchmark utility transmission capex and lead-time evidence.

The node appears investable through three public-market mappings: direct line hardware suppliers, broader connector/fitting incumbents, and second-order structure/coating suppliers tied to the same transmission BOM.

summary: Layer 1B expansion for the transmission-line hardware node found one unusually direct underfollowed public candidate, PLPC, plus three adjacent public-market mappings that may benefit from the same transmission-capex chokepoint. The strongest node fit is qualified line hardware and OPGW/conductor-adjacent components. The next-best second-order fits are transmission connectors, utility structures, and galvanizing/corrosion-protection services required for transmission infrastructure.
